as_told.title: Puharich case of metal in teeth picking up signals

plain: The story goes that a man who said he heard voices turned out to be picking up a radio station through fine metal dust lodged in his teeth. It is linked to Andrija Puharich, a researcher of the paranormal who ran a lab in New York in the 1950s and 60s. A researcher named Greg Malatzi, drawing on the writer Annie Jacobsen, calls it Puharich's "first aha moment": "they got a mental patient, a guy who claimed he was hearing voices." The station is identified as New York's WOR. Michels brings it up himself in three other episodes, with details that shift: the man worked in "some metal sawmill or something" or "a metal mill," and "metallic ore got in his teeth." Once Michels says he got it from a documentary on Puharich and ties it to the idea of sending thoughts by ELF, extremely low frequency radio waves. None of Michels's versions names the station. It is told because, if true, it would show the human body acting as a receiver for signals, which feeds ideas about transmitting thought.
